  PROBLEM: A raw read written after `elif`, after a case-pattern `)`, or as `<(gh api ...)` / `(gh api ...)` is not recognised as a call; no current line uses these forms.
  WHY: Suggested fix: add `elif|until` to the keyword group, allow `\(` without trailing whitespace after `<` or at line start, and add one self-test line per form; about 4 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_gh_rate_limit_routing.py:_WRITE_FLAG regex at line 150; _is_raw_read() body at lines 174-180 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_WRITE_FLAG` matches write flags anywhere in `rest` with no quote handling, so a read whose `--jq` filter contains `-f ` and that has no `-X`/`--method` hits `if _WRITE_FLAG.search(rest) and not method`, which returns False and marks it as a write.
  WHY: Such a read passes the contract test with no allowlist entry; the new position-aware path (`_unlisted_reads` → `_raw_read_positions` → `_is_raw_read`) inherits the misclassification, and `test_scanner_recognises_reads_and_writes` never tests this case.

  PROBLEM: The command-start context class leaves out `}` and `)` (case-pattern end), so a raw `gh` call directly after either token is not detected.
  WHY: Suggested fix: extend `[;|&!{`]` to `[;|&!{}()]` in both patterns; about 2 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
